issues.display_title: Issue #1903: Allow Subsequent Stitching Jobs on Existing Tours & Fix Unlock Payment Check
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Fix an issue where users are blocked from submitting a new auto-stitch job for a virtual tour that previously completed a stitching job. The checkout/unlock flow fails with the error: Auto Stitch Unlock Failed - Reason for Failure: Payment has already been processed for this item. (Reported by user Stephen Young on tour Stitching Account (sx_ZmN0d2KjKSK1B11h3J)).

Result (Implementation Proof)

1. Root Cause Analysis

  • Location: app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/OneTimePayment/UnlockStitching.php (lines 66–72).
  • Cause: A pre-charge guard checked the unlocked_cid_stich table by user_id and cid: 
    $alreadyUnlocked = $this->databaseClass->tableUnlockedCidStich()
    ->where(\x27user_id\x27, $preparedData[\x27user_id\x27])
    ->where(\x27cid\x27, $preparedData[\x27moderation_info\x27][\x271_cid\x27])
    ->exists();
if ($alreadyUnlocked) {
    throw new \\Exception(__(\x27messages.payment.payment_already_processed\x27), 409);
}
  • Why It Failed for Subsequent Jobs: Unlike Publishing (which is one-time per CID), Auto Stitching allows multiple and subsequent stitching jobs for the same tour / CID over time (e.g., adding more panoramas, re-running stitching). When a user (e.g., Stephen Young on tour sx_ZmN0d2KjKSK1B11h3J) submits a subsequent stitching job for a tour where stitching was previously unlocked, a row already exists in unlocked_cid_stich, causing the pre-charge guard to throw HTTP 409 (Payment has already been processed for this item.).
  • Database & Alur Bukti:
    • In unlocked_cid_stich, multiple historical records with the same (user_id, cid) exist by design across different timestamps.
    • The PayPal counterpart (CaptureOrder.php / prepareUnlockStitching) does not block by CID, confirming this was an unintentional blocker in the Stripe action.

2. Implementation Details & Code Diff

Removed the unlocked_cid_stich check and cleaned up the unused DatabaseClass dependency in UnlockStitching.php:

--- a/app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/OneTimePayment/UnlockStitching.php
+++ b/app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/OneTimePayment/UnlockStitching.php
@@ -6,7 +6,6 @@ use Illuminate\\Support\\Facades\\Validator;
 use Illuminate\\Http\\Request;
 use App\\Class\\HelperClass;
 use App\\Class\\Payment\\StripeClass;
-use App\\Class\\DatabaseClass;
 use App\\Http\\Controllers\\Payment\\Helpers\\OneTimePayment\\UnlockStitchingHelpers;
 use Stripe\\Exception\\ApiErrorException;
 
@@ -14,14 +13,12 @@ class UnlockStitching
 {
     private $helperClass;
     private $stripeClass;
-    private $databaseClass;
     private $unlockStitchingHelpers;
 
     public function __construct()
     {
         $this->helperClass = new HelperClass();
         $this->stripeClass = new StripeClass();
-        $this->databaseClass = new DatabaseClass();
         $this->unlockStitchingHelpers = new UnlockStitchingHelpers();
     }
 
@@ -61,16 +58,6 @@ class UnlockStitching
             // Validate and prepare unlock stitching (reusable for both Stripe and PayPal)
             $preparedData = $this->unlockStitchingHelpers->validateAndPrepareUnlockStitching($request, $isTestMode);
 
-            // Key the guard on the true unlock evidence (unlocked_cid_stich insert), not
-            // the 0_moderation.is_stich_payed flag which can persist after a failed attempt.
-            $alreadyUnlocked = $this->databaseClass->tableUnlockedCidStich()
-                ->where(\x27user_id\x27, $preparedData[\x27user_id\x27])
-                ->where(\x27cid\x27, $preparedData[\x27moderation_info\x27][\x271_cid\x27])
-                ->exists();
-            if ($alreadyUnlocked) {
-                throw new \\Exception(__(\x27messages.payment.payment_already_processed\x27), 409);
-            }
-
             // Prepare metadata for Stripe
             $metadata = [];

3. Pull Request & Merged Changes

  • PR: #1909 (fix(payment): remove unlocked_cid_stich guard to allow multiple unlock stitching)
  • Status: Merged to main (45a138a79)

4. Verification

  • PHP Syntax & Lint: Passed without errors: 
    php -l app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/OneTimePayment/UnlockStitching.php
# Output: No syntax errors detected
  • Local Working Copy: Up to date with origin/main.

issues.display_title: Issue #1911: Fix First-Character Truncation on Recipient Email for Invoice Notifications
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Investigate and resolve an issue where the leading character of the recipient's email address is truncated during email preparation or dispatch, causing delivery failures (HARD FAIL). In this incident, user_id: 33141 has the registered email fernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com in the database, but the outgoing message was dispatched to ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com (missing the leading 'f').

Investigation Report (Root Cause & Evidence)

Date: September 18, 2026
Target Transaction: BOPP12400049 (user_id = 33141)
Status: Resolved via PR #1913

1. Executive Summary & Root Cause

  • Hypothesis: Leading character truncation during email preparation/dispatch in the application code.
  • Investigation Finding: No string truncation (substr/regex) occurred in the backend.
  • Root Cause Details:
    1. Transaction BOPP12400049 is a legacy Payflow Pro recurring transaction processed by RecordPayflowRecurringTransactionsHelper.php.
    2. The cronjob did not query the gothru_mod.users table for the recipient email. Instead, it followed this priority chain:
      • Priority 1: billing_addresses.billing_email in gothru_mod.
      • Priority 2 (Fallback): $transaction['Billing Email'] provided directly by PayPal Payflow Pro reporting engine.
    3. In gothru_mod.billing_addresses, the record for user_id = 33141 has an empty string ("") in billing_email.
    4. The cronjob therefore fell back to the email returned by the PayPal Payflow Reporting Engine API, which returned "Billing Email": "ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com" (missing the f).
    5. PayPal's Payflow Pro Recurring Profile (RP0000003802) has contained this typo on PayPal's end since March 17, 2026 (Payment 36) when the subscriber's payment details were updated.

2. Evidence: Raw Response from PayPal Payflow Reporting Engine API

Direct query to PayPal Payflow Reporting API (https://payments-reports.paypal.com/reportingengine, Template Logs) for transaction BOPP12400049:

    <columnData colNum="12"><data>Recurring Profile: RP0000003802 Payment: 000042 Name: recurring_for_user_33141</data></columnData>

3. Database Evidence

FROM ccdb.cc_logs_paypal

ORDER BY log_id ASC;
  • Payments 01 to 35 (2023-04-17 to 2026-02-17):
    PayPal returned billing_email: nanditon1@hotmail.com.
  • Payments 36 to 42 (2026-03-17 to 2026-09-17):
    PayPal returned billing_email: ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com.
    • Payment 36 (2026-03-17, BDPP1BCAADD2): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com
    • Payment 37 (2026-04-17, BDPP1C0D7FA1): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com
    • Payment 38 (2026-05-17, BPPPA106BA0E): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com
    • Payment 39 (2026-06-17, BVPP1C52E009): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com
    • Payment 40 (2026-07-17, BDPP1C8F4DC3): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com
    • Payment 41 (2026-08-17, BVPP1C8421DB): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com
    • Payment 42 (2026-09-17, BOPP12400049): ernandobellodelcastillo@gmail.com

4. Code Resolution (Pull Request #1913)

Implemented a robust email resolution mechanism across all recurring payment cronjobs in PR #1913:

Priority Order:

1. billing_addresses.billing_email  (Custom billing email if explicitly set and valid)
2. users.email                      (Primary verified account email in GoThru)
3. Gateway metadata                 (Fallback: receipt_email / subscriber_email / payer_email)

Components Implemented:

  1. App\Http\Controllers\Cronjobs\Helpers\InvoiceRecipientEmailResolver:
    • Validates each candidate using filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL).
    • Ensures corrupted/typo gateway metadata is bypassed whenever a valid users.email exists.
  2. Helper Updates:
    • RecordPayflowRecurringTransactionsHelper
    • RecordPaypalRecurringTransactionsHelper
    • RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper
      Each helper caches users.email per run and delegates recipient email selection to the resolver.
  3. Unit Tests & E2E Verification:
    • tests/Helpers/Cronjobs/InvoiceRecipientEmailResolverTest.php (6 tests, 8 assertions, 100% OK).
    • tests/Routes/RecordPayflowRecurringTransactionsDryRunTest.php (2 tests, 23 assertions, 100% OK).

issues.display_title: Issue #1914: feat(maps-javascript): create paginated endpoint GET /users/map-javascript/{id}/tours
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation MapsJavascript — Get Map Javascript Tours

GET /users/map-javascript/{id}/tours

Auth: middleware('auth')

Used By: gothru-dashboard

Flow:

  1. Request enters → GetMapJavascriptToursController@handle builds GetMapJavascriptToursDto from route {id}, $request->user_id, and query parameters (page, limit, search).
  2. Controller delegates to GetMapJavascriptToursAction::execute(GetMapJavascriptToursDto).
  3. Action runs business logic:
    • Queries MapsJavascriptRepository::getKeyById(keyId) — if not found, throws MapsJavascriptNotFoundException (404)
    • Checks if authenticated user owns the key (user_id == key['user_id']) — if not, throws MapsJavascriptNotOwnerException (403)
    • Parses tour moderation IDs from google_api_keys.tours via MapsJavascriptRepository::parseTourIds()
    • Queries MapsJavascriptRepository::getToursByMapKey() for user's tours matching the parsed IDs or containing the key ID in tours.api_key_id, applying search and pagination
    • Formats tour records with mid, name, tour_key and pagination metadata (page, limit, total, total_page)
    • Returns tours[] and pagination
  4. Controller receives result → wraps into JSON response:
    • Success → ResponseEnvelopeHelper::rawResponse() (200)
    • MapsJavascriptDomainException → MapsJavascriptExceptionHttpMapper → ResponseEnvelopeHelper::errorResponse() with mapped status
    • \Throwable → ResponseEnvelopeHelper::errorResponseFromThrowable()

DTO (app/DTOs/MapsJavascript/GetMapJavascriptToursDto.php):

Field Type Source Notes
keyId int {id} Route parameter
userId int $request->user_id Injected by auth middleware
page int $request->query('page') Optional, default 1
limit int $request->query('limit') Optional, default 10, max 100
search ?string $request->query('search') Optional, searches across tour_name, moderation_id, and tour_key

Response (200):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "tours": [
      {
        "mid": 3556442,
        "name": "Warung Jawa Timur Bu Joko, Rawa Terate",
        "tour_key": "DOIbSymI"
      }
    ],
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "limit": 10,
      "total": 1,
      "total_page": 1
    }
  }
}

Errors:

domainCode HTTP Condition
MAPS_JAVASCRIPT.NOT_FOUND 404 When key ID does not exist
MAPS_JAVASCRIPT.NOT_OWNER 403 When key belongs to a different user

Usage:

curl -X GET "https://api.gothru.co/users/map-javascript/123/tours?page=1&limit=10&search=Warung" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Compliance Status: 100% (Strict ADR)

Summary

Implement a dedicated paginated endpoint GET /users/map-javascript/{id}/tours to fetch the list of virtual tours using a specific Maps JavaScript API key on demand.

Background

To support the modal view on the frontend dashboard (/profile/map-javascript), users need to see all virtual tours using a specific API key with search and pagination capabilities, without overloading the master key list endpoint.

Specification

Endpoint: GET /users/map-javascript/{id}/tours

  • Auth: Required (Bearer <token>)
  • Route Params: id (int, ID of the Google API Key)
  • Query Params:
    • page (optional, default: 1)
    • limit (optional, default: 10)
    • search (optional, search across tour_name, moderation_id, or tour_key)

Response Format:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "tours": [
      {
        "mid": 3556442,
        "name": "Warung Jawa Timur Bu Joko, Rawa Terate",
        "tour_key": "DOIbSymI"
      }
    ],
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "limit": 10,
      "total": 1,
      "total_page": 1
    }
  }
}

Security & Verification

  • Verify ownership of the key (user_id must match authenticated user). Return 404 or 403 if invalid.
  • Parse tour IDs from google_api_keys.tours or query hosted_tours.tours where api_key_id contains key ID.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Route registered in routes/userRoutes.php.
  • Controller / Action / Repository layer implemented following project standards.
  • Pagination (page, limit, total, total_page) functioning accurately.
  • Search filtering functioning on tour name, MID, and tour key.
  • Unit & E2E tests covering authorized, unauthorized, empty, and paginated cases.

issues.display_title: Issue #1912: feat(maps-javascript): include usage status and tours count in GET /users/map-javascript
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation MapsJavascript — Get Map Javascript

GET /users/map-javascript

Auth: middleware('auth')

Used By: gothru-dashboard

Flow:

  1. Request enters → GetMapJavascriptController@handle builds GetMapJavascriptDto from $request->user_id (middleware).
  2. Controller delegates to GetMapJavascriptAction::execute(GetMapJavascriptDto).
  3. Action runs business logic:
    • Delegates to MapsJavascriptRepository::getKeysByUserId(userId) — queries hosted_tours.google_api_keys for id, name, key, usage_location, tours where user_id = ?
    • Computes usage_status (in_use for global or count >= 1; unused otherwise) and tours_count, strips raw tours column, and returns maps[] array of key records
  4. Controller receives result → wraps into JSON response:
    • Success → encryptResult() with last_login, encrypt, and maps
    • MapsJavascriptDomainException → MapsJavascriptExceptionHttpMapper → responseMessages()
    • \Throwable → statusCodeFromThrowable() → responseMessages()

DTO (app/DTOs/MapsJavascript/GetMapJavascriptDto.php):

Field Type Source Notes
userId int $request->user_id Injected by auth middleware

Response (200):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "messages": "Data retrieved",
    "last_login": "2026-05-26T10:00:00Z",
    "encrypt": "<encrypted_payload>"
  }
}

Decrypted payload:

{
  "maps": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "My Key",
      "key": "AIzaSy...",
      "usage_location": "tour",
      "usage_status": "in_use",
      "tours_count": 3
    }
  ]
}

Errors:

domainCode HTTP Condition
(any mapped code) varies MapsJavascriptExceptionHttpMapper resolves known domain exceptions; defaults to 400 for unrecognised codes

Usage:

curl -X GET "https://api.gothru.co/users/map-javascript" \
  -H "Authorization: <token>"

Compliance Status: 100% (Strict ADR)

Remarks: Fully migrated from legacy User\MapsJavascript\Action\GetMapJavascript with preserved logic flow (auth user id -> fetch keys -> encrypted response envelope). Data access now isolated in MapsJavascriptRepository on hosted_tours.google_api_keys. Action is fully HTTP-free and has zero dependency on legacy business/data classes. Response remains encrypted via ResponseEnvelopeHelper::encryptResult() at controller transport edge. MapsJavascriptRepository uses Laravel's native DatabaseManager — zero App\Class dependency at any layer.

Summary

Enhance the master GET /users/map-javascript endpoint to return lightweight usage status and tour counts per API key.

Background

On the dashboard page (/profile/map-javascript), users need to see which keys are actively in use and how many virtual tours rely on each key, without downloading full tour records up front.

Specification

Endpoint: GET /users/map-javascript

Add the following fields to each key item in data.maps[]:

{
  "id": 2815424,
  "name": "Client_Project_Alpha_Map",
  "key": "AIzaSy...",
  "usage_location": "tour",
  "usage_status": "in_use",
  "tours_count": 3
}
  • usage_status: "in_use" | "unused"
    • For usage_location = 'global': marked as "in_use".
    • For usage_location = 'tour': marked as "in_use" if assigned to 1 or more virtual tours; otherwise "unused".
  • tours_count: int (count of assigned virtual tours).

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /users/map-javascript includes usage_status and tours_count per key.
  • Maintains backward compatibility with existing consumers (dropdowns and mobile views).
  • Fast database query execution without full tour data joins.
  • Unit & repository test coverage.
